value.answer: For most adults, short-term use looks fine. The NIH says it appears safe for most people, and UC Davis says it's typically well tolerated at low doses when used for the shortest time, meaning one to two months. Long-term safety is less clear. A new AHA abstract from November 2025 linked a year or more of use in chronic insomnia to more heart failure, but it's preliminary, not peer-reviewed, can't prove cause, and some experts think poor sleep could explain it. Older adults and anyone with a history of fractures should be extra careful, since there may be a fracture risk. Sources also disagree on the right dose, so ask a doctor or pharmacist about yours, especially if you take other medications.
